How Much House Can I Afford?

Buying a home is one of the biggest financial decisions many people make. Estimating an affordable home price can help you understand what monthly payment may fit your budget before you start comparing properties.

Ad space (in-content)

What determines how much house you can afford?

Several factors affect how much home you may be able to afford, including your income, existing debts, down payment, mortgage interest rate, property taxes, homeowners insurance, and other housing costs.

A higher income or larger down payment can increase the amount you may be able to afford, while higher interest rates, taxes, insurance, or existing debt can reduce your affordable price.

Consider the complete monthly housing cost

The mortgage principal and interest payment is only part of the cost of owning a home. Your monthly housing expenses may also include property taxes, homeowners insurance, homeowners association fees, and private mortgage insurance when applicable.

Looking at the complete estimated housing payment can give you a more realistic picture of what a home may cost each month.

How a down payment affects affordability

A larger down payment reduces the amount you need to borrow. This can lower the monthly principal and interest payment and reduce the amount of interest paid over the life of the mortgage.

A smaller down payment may allow you to purchase a home sooner, but it can result in a larger loan balance and may introduce additional costs such as private mortgage insurance.
